what: Comet plot for paired or multi-step measurements from a phyloseq object — comet_pq
title: Comet plot for paired or multi-step measurements from a phyloseq object — comet_pq
text: comet plot (also called tapered-line slope arrow plot) visualises paired multi-step continuous measurements observational unit. linewidth-tapered segment (path) connects origin destination: narrow end origin wide end destination. Vocabulary comet full path drawn one observational unit. defined sequence (x, y, modality_level) observations sharing id value. id level defines exactly one comet. step one node (x, y) along comet, corresponding one level modality ordered factor. Duplicate modality levels within id allowed. tail first step (smallest modality level); tip last step (largest modality level). path tapers thin tail thick tip. Two interfaces supported: Wide format (x_start, x_end, y_start, y_end): row data holds start end coordinates. Uses ggforce::geom_link() draw single tapered segment per row. Long format (x, y, modality, id): row holds one measurement one observational unit one modality level. modality must ordered factor 2 levels; id identifies unit. Uses ggforce::geom_link2() linewidth tapers continuously across steps (independently per segment), enabling timeline-style multi-step comets. title: Ternary and diamond plots for 3-or-4-group taxon compositions — ternary_pq
text: Displays taxon point inside triangle (3 groups) diamond (4 groups) whose corners represent sample groups. taxon plotted near one corner abundant group. coordinate math follows standard de Finetti diagram (Wikipedia: Ternary plot): $$x = \frac{2b + c}{2(+b+c)}, \quad y = \frac{\sqrt{3}\,c}{2(+b+c)}$$ \(,b,c\) mean relative abundances left, right, top groups respectively. diamond projection 4 groups uses: $$x = \frac{- c}{+b+c+d}, \quad y = \frac{b - d}{+b+c+d}$$ (right, top, left, bottom). independent implementation; coordinate formulas public domain (de Finetti 1926; see also Armstrong 2014, IEEE VIS).
